verification.note: fileops.py:667-673 physical_delete calls existing_or_409 (strict). That raises HTTP 409 on an ambiguous name. In purge_all_trash (fileops.py:756-759) the loop unlinks and db.delete+flush each file, and the one commit comes after the loop. A 409 on a later file leaves earlier files unlinked on disk while their rows roll back, so the DB points at deleted files. Before the change nothing raised here. purge_all_missing (786-815) is batched, so the exposure is one batch of 200.

Same as claude-read F1. purge_all_trash commits once after the loop (fileops.py:759) while physical_delete unlinks at 672-673 after the strict resolve at 670. I did not open main.py:96, so the per-row commit claim for the purge job is unchecked.

The facts hold: uploads.py:84 uses asyncio.to_thread, and markdown_image_import.py:552-592 now has prepare_import and launch_import beside start_import. It is a scope and process observation, not a defect, and the touch-point scope rule covers sites the inventory reports. Not checked: whether behaviour changed. Low risk.

upload.py:247-248 uses new_or_409 (strict) on the parent and resolve_on_disk non-strict on the leaf. This is the in-place replacement that I7 specifies for a destination existing in the other spelling. I12's 409 rule lists only rename, move, delete, purge and restore, not upload. Replacement goes through replacing_file (upload.py:258), which is atomic. Under the single-user threat model this is not a defect.
